attributes.residual: THE WORK ORDER'S OWN FRAMING IS HALF-REFUTED AND THE MECHANISM IS NOW NAMED. The order states the 48+16 dead regions are 'UNRECOVERED REAL LOCALS interleaved with the temp pool'. Measurement splits that claim: the 16 dead bytes at r1+88..103 ARE a declared local and our `u8 stackLayout[16]` reproduces that half exactly; the 40 dead bytes at r1+16..55 are NOT a local and cannot be one, because MWCC anchors a four-slot memory-temp group at the local-area base (r1+16/20/24/28) that NO declared object -- inner-block or function-scope, first- or last-declared, 4 to 56 bytes -- is ever allocated below. That is measured four ways this run and eight times in total counting the FR/CB probes. The correct model of both frames is: declared locals pack DOWNWARD from the top of the local area, the temp allocator fills the gap directly beneath the lowest declared object and spills to the base group when that gap is exhausted, and local_area = roundup16(content) with frame = 16 + local_area + 104. The target's temp base is 56 and ours is 16; since the region below the local area is only the outgoing parameter area, the remaining 40 bytes are either parameter space (forbidden for this call set by the CI law, whose one untested sub-case is named in the hypothesis) or allocator slack with no source lever. DO NOT re-probe any declared-pad placement, at any scope -- that axis is now closed with a named mechanism rather than an empirical tally. The two-buffer split remains reproducible and correct in ARRANGEMENT (probe 2 seats sp0 above sp1 as the target does) but is worthless while the base is 40 bytes low, and it regresses real on its own, so it must be re-applied only in the same edit that fixes the base.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: HARNESS ONLY, no edit to combat.c: extend tools/gdl/composed_census/ci_paramarea_probe.py with one case that calls a callee taking a 40-byte struct BY VALUE (e.g. `struct S40 { int a[10]; }; void f(struct S40);`) under combat.c's cflags, and read the resulting outgoing parameter area as (lowest occupied r1 slot - 8). If the area stays at 8 -- i.e. MWCC materialises the aggregate in a LOCAL temp and passes a pointer, or copies it through the temp pool rather than the parameter area -- then this hypothesis is dead, the CI law stands unqualified at every struct size, and the 40 bytes are pure allocator slack with NO source-level lever, which converts this function from CAPPED to a permanent source-unreachable park eligible for the postprocessor provenance bar. Note the observation targets THIS record's own mechanism (aggregate-sized parameter area), not the already-refuted register-argument-count mechanism.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - measured from the target's own bytes this run, not inherited. Every N(r1) displacement in the target's 199 instructions was enumerated: the occupied set is {4, 56, 60, 64, 68, 72, 76, 80, 82, 84, 86, 104, 108, 112, 116, 120, 124, 128, 232, 236}. r1+8..55 and r1+88..103 are therefore confirmed NEVER read and NEVER written, independently reproducing the CB/CI finding. The target's six 4-use f32 temps sit at 56..76 and its two s16[2] buffers at 80/82 and 84/86, so the target's temp base is 56 against our 16.
hypothesis.statement: The 40 bytes are NOT source-declarable, so the only remaining source-reachable mechanism is a LARGER OUTGOING PARAMETER AREA, and the one sub-case the run-34 refutation harness never sized is a callee taking a LARGE STRUCT BY VALUE. claim.law.CI_mwcc-outgoing-param-area-is-sized-only-by-stack-spilled-args.20260902.v1 reports that a struct-by-value argument 'does not reach 48', but its record never states the STRUCT SIZE tested; a by-value aggregate is copied into the caller's outgoing parameter area, so a >=40-byte struct argument should reserve >=40 bytes there regardless of GPR count. If that holds, the original's MBWindowProject-family prototype passed an aggregate by value and the entire 40-byte base shift, the pool base, both s16 buffers and all 34 IMMEDIATE displacement rows follow by construction.
